label: early copy step echoing q/w/l/c (recall 1-2), sparse subset
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the first two copy steps after <DEL> (recall_idx 1: 63% of mass; recall_idx 2: 35%), when the fed-back input token is q, w, l or c (about 93% of mass). Strongest when that token is the first original token, i.e. the step right after <DEL>, and the top examples often have p/r/f/h coming up in the original sequence. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on a first occurrence of a token. The context predicate gets about 90% of activation mass, but precision is only about 1.6%: the feature fires on just a few percent of matching steps, and which ones depends on a spread-out combination of the later original tokens (next_out p/r/f/h, several of p/r/f/h at positions 2-5) that no simple predicate captures. The best refinement reached F1 about 0.16. Magnitude is fairly flat (median 0.12, max 0.23).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=q (+5.52), phase=2 & in_tok=l (+4.70), phase=2 & in_tok=w (+4.45), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+3.90), phase=2 & out_tok=g (+3.33), orig2=p (+2.57). Lower it: orig4=w (-2.91), orig3=2 (-2.85), orig5=c (-2.70), orig3=c (-2.64).
